summary: Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned a Shastri and Acharya at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed her PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He served as abbot at Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery, and founded Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling (1973) and Tekchen Lekshay Ling (1988).

Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College (~1980–1983), Magdalen College, Oxford (~1983–1986), and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (1999–2008).

Karsé Kongtrul studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Khakyab Dorje, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He also taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and later served as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Karunapati Tripathi was an Indologist. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as President of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan.

Karunesh Shukla is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied under V. P. Upadhyaya. He held posts as Reader (attested 1973) and Professor (attested 1991) at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation.

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. She earned her degrees and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, later serving as full professor (from 1999) and dean (2007–2010) at the University of Bern.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Lincoln's Inn, and Oxford. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India (~1937).

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Officiating Government Epigraphist for India (~1931–1932), Deputy Director-General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1944), and held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indologist educated at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1892–1893) and president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1892–1893).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1916–1945) and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1956–1976).

Kate Crosby works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts at St Peter's College, Oxford, Cardiff University, the Buddhist Institute (2003), SOAS University of London, and King's College London (attested 2026).

Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London in 2008 and held an affiliation with Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. She completed her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul works in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann, as well as Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.
Katherine K. Young is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago and McGill University, where she became a professor around 1978.

Kathleen D. Morrison works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She served as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern (~1994–1995) and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).
